Theta GmbH's strategy of filing for multiple patents on next-generation wireless communication is a high-impact move that creates significant barriers to entry. By securing a temporary monopoly on specific technologies, they are effectively locking out competitors from using those particular innovations without licensing agreements. This directly impedes our development efforts by forcing us to either navigate complex licensing negotiations, which can be costly and time-consuming, or to pivot our R&D toward alternative solutions. While seeking alternatives may delay our time-to-market, it also presents an opportunity to innovate around their patents, potentially leading to unique differentiators if we can develop superior or distinct technologies that do not infringe on their claims.

A book is primarily made of paper.
